title: Data Residency: Where Does Your List Actually Live?
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: Ask your email platform where subscriber data sits and the answer is a shrug and a subprocessors page. Self-hosting turns the answer into an address you chose.
content:
"Where is my subscribers' data stored?" For most email platforms the honest answer is a list of regions, subprocessors and clauses. When you self-host, the answer is one sentence: on my server, in the jurisdiction I picked.

Why residency keeps coming up

Privacy regulators care about where personal data crosses borders, and so do an increasing number of customers. Enterprise procurement teams now ask residency questions in the first call. A mailing list is personal data - names, emails, behavior - so residency is not an abstract concern for anyone who sends email.

What self-hosting changes

You choose the datacenter and the country. Backups live where you put them. Access logs are yours. When a customer or a regulator asks where the data is, you answer from knowledge, not from a vendor's marketing page. That answer - specific, verifiable, yours - builds a kind of trust no badge can.

The obligations that stay yours

Residency is not a compliance certificate. Consent records, unsubscribe handling, deletion requests and breach duties remain your job under GDPR and friends. Self-hosting makes the geography simple; the discipline is still on you.

A question worth asking today

Wherever your list lives now, find the answer in your vendor's documentation. If it takes more than five minutes to find, that is the answer.
